free_tier.stated: No free tier. VPS - NAT512 is USD 7.50 a year: 512 MB RAM, 5 GB SSD, 1 CPU core on fair use, a /80 IPv6 plus a NAT IPv4 with 20 usable ports and 1 SSH port, 750 GB transfer a month. Sold per location; the NAT768 at USD 10 a year (768 MB RAM, 7 GB SSD, 1024 GB a month) is the only other rung. Stock is a dated observation of the cart pages, not a property of either plan: on 2026-10-24 and again on 2026-10-30 the NAT512 card carried no out-of-stock badge and the NAT768 card carried 'Out of stock' at each of eight locations: France, Canada, Netherlands, Norway, New York, Los Angeles, Singapore and Japan.

retention.stated: annual prepay; the terms state 'All services are invoiced 10 days before due date. Unpaid services are suspended 3 days after due date. Unpaid services are terminated 5 days after due date, all data is deleted and cannot be recovered.'

egress.terms: the monthly transfer allowance is enforced by disabling the server: a server that uses up all of its monthly allowed bandwidth becomes DISABLED and is reactivated automatically on the first day of the next month; a warning email and portal notification go out at 80 percent of the assigned traffic and again when the server is disabled
egress.price_per_tb: USD 8 a year adds 1 TB of transfer to the monthly allowance, which is USD 0.67 per added TB when it is used every month

interface_detail: KVM guest with root over SSH; the NAT IPv4 ports and the public IPv4 are listed in the control panel's Network tab, and a knowledge-base article walks through finding them. No panel for changing the mapping is documented: the ports are assigned, not chosen.
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor's own FAQ recommends 'road warrior WireGuard-installer script for easy setup'
chaining: 512 MB and 5 GB for USD 0.625 a month is the largest shape found under the dollar line, and the vendor's FAQ answers the WireGuard question in one line: 'Yes, it can!'

limits.value: 20 usable ports on a shared NAT IPv4 plus 1 SSH port; the ports are assigned by the provider, not configured by the buyer
annual prepay only at this rung, as read on 2026-10-30: USD 7.50 is the first payment and the smallest term

binding_note: 750 GB a month is about 25 GB a day, which a tunnel will not reach but a monitoring host with a chatty probe might; the port count is the second constraint and the price is not one.

identity_cost.detail: email address, password and an image captcha, read from the order form's inputs, which are username, password and captcha only. No card, address, phone or ID field is on the order form; payment is collected after the account exists. No card hold is stated anywhere read. The order page warns 'Turn off your VPN before placing an order'.

reliability_note: the FAQ states 'Due to the low cost nature of service, we cannot provide SLA' and 'We strive to maintain 99.9% uptime at all locations'; the status page showed the Canada and France KVM nodes at 100 percent on 2026-10-24; the provider bars Tor, torrents, crypto mining and port scanning and caps sustained CPU at 50 percent of a core over 24 hours

notes: USD 7.50 a year is USD 0.625 a month for 512 MB and 5 GB. Stock is dated: the cart pages read on 2026-10-24 and on 2026-10-30 showed the NAT512 card without an out-of-stock badge and the NAT768 card marked 'Out of stock' at each of eight locations, so the seller's stock flag is per plan and per location; a later read can differ. The WireGuard question is answered by the vendor in one line on its own home page, which is a sentence about capability, not a measurement, and no page states UDP on the forwarded ports. The 20 NAT ports are assigned, not chosen: the knowledge base tells a buyer to read the port list from the Network tab, and no page describes changing a mapping. Entity: the footer gives 'Registered Name - NatVPS Services' and a GSTIN whose check digit validates under the GSTIN algorithm and whose state code is Maharashtra; it was not checked against the Indian GST portal. A tracker row naming WebHorizon IT Broadband Limited as the owner is not confirmed. Not established: UDP on the forwarded ports, whether the assigned ports can be changed, and the payment rails at checkout, because the gateway list appears only after the account exists.
